items.Sentence: Wastewater from the town of Julian initially flows through an eight-inch sewer main into the equalization tank for pre-treatment.
The headworks are housed in a 5 feet x 10 feet below-grade concrete tank, with dual channels and bar screens.

Afterwards, the wastewater flows into the aeration tanks. The aeration tanks consist of two 53 feet x 53 feet below-grade concrete basins, each equipped with a floating mechanical aerator to facilitate complete mix, extended aeration secondary treatment.
The wastewater then flows to the secondary clarifiers for sludge settling and removal, which consist of two 18 feet diameter concrete tanks.
The RAS/WAS pump station is comprised of two rotary lobe pumps housed in a concrete vault capable of returning or wasting the settled sludge from the secondary clarifiers.
The aerobic digesters are two 18 feet x 18 feet above-ground concrete tanks where the sludge digestion process is completed.
Once digestion is complete, the WAS is sent to the Sludge Drying Beds until it becomes dry enough to haul away to an appropriate landfill.

The storage basins are below-grade concrete lined ponds with a total capacity of 225,000 cubic feet of storage, roughly equal to 67 days of treated effluent at an average daily flow rate of 25,000 gallons per day (gpd).
The clarified effluent is pumped to an adjacent field on the site and used for spray irrigation.
